cases.title: Property: validate_format agrees with a model written from the spec text and a direct git call
cases.given: 1500 formats per seed: half from testkit arb.format (braces, unicode whitespace, control chars, NUL, lone surrogates, non-strings), half one-placeholder formats with git-unsafe literals
cases.when: validate_format(fmt) is compared with the model: non-string, placeholder count != 1, brace outside the placeholder, Unicode White_Space, then git check-ref-format --branch on the S-001 candidate
cases.then: the verdicts agree; a git refusal carries check-ref-format and git's reason; no other exception
cases.expected: Fail or the exact input as the model says; no exception
cases.actual: 0 violations for seed 20261009 (448 accepted) and seed 777123 (458 accepted), 1500 runs each
cases.specSource: R-017 quote and acceptance; R-001 quote

cases.title: Literal parts that git refuses raise Fail with git's reason, the same verdict as a direct git call
cases.given: 24 formats with .., .lock, leading - or /, trailing / or ., //, ~ ^ : ? * [ \, /.b, control chars, DEL, NUL, --format/ and -h prefixes, and @/
cases.when: validate_format(fmt), then git check-ref-format --branch on the same candidate
cases.then: verdicts match; the message holds check-ref-format and git's reason text
cases.expected: Fail with git's reason for each git-refused candidate; @/{name} accepted by both
cases.actual: all verdicts match git. 21 messages carry 'check-ref-format' and git's reason. \x1f fails on the whitespace check (Python \s). NUL fails with 'embedded null byte'. A leading dash is refused by git as a name, not read as an option
cases.specSource: R-017 acceptance (the invalid-ref rejection carries git check-ref-format's reason)

seeds.title: Zero-width and BOM characters pass validate_format
seeds.detail: validate_format accepts formats with U+200B, U+200C, U+200D, U+FEFF and U+180E, because they are not Unicode whitespace and git accepts them. A branch name can then hold an invisible character. The spec forbids only whitespace. Consider a refusal of Unicode format characters (category Cf).

seeds.title: The first git on PATH decides the validate_format verdict
seeds.detail: A fake git on PATH that exits 0 makes validate_format accept sdlc/{name}... The spec does not define which git runs. Consider a note in the pre-flight output that names the git binary, or a check of git --version.

seeds.title: Control characters U+001C to U+001F fail as whitespace
seeds.detail: Python re \s matches U+001C to U+001F, so validate_format refuses a\x1f/{name} with 'holds whitespace' and not with git's control-character reason. The verdict is correct. Only the message text is misleading.
